newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNITED SWEAT ON PALLISTER INJURY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED SWEAT ON PALLISTER INJURY.

text.p: Norwegian defender Ronny Johnsen is set to replace the injured Gary Pallister as Manchester United attempt to shrug off their recent premier league form for Wednesday's Champions' League home clash with Fenerbahce.
Pallister limped out of Saturday's 6-3 defeat at Southampton with a knee injury and has had constant treatment since then.
United manager Alex Ferguson says Pallister is still "very doubtful" for the group match, although Johnsen is fit again after treatment on an Achilles injury and can step into the side.
Midfielder Nicky Butt, another of United's doubts who came off after 17 minutes at The Dell with a damaged knee, went jogging on Monday and was hoping to have a chance of facing the Turks.
United are trying to become the first British club to qualify for the quarter-final stage of the European Cup since the introduction of the league system.
But Ferguson said: "At the moment Pallister is not looking good for Wednesday and Butt has not got much chance either. Both are very doubtful.
"Pallister's injury is something that will just not go away. He has probably twisted his knee and tweaked the ligaments.
"We need to give him a couple of weeks off to let it clear up completely, but with an important game coming up like this one we also need to get him fit."
United beat Fenerbahce 2-0 in Istanbul two weeks ago and have never lost at home in 40 years of European competition.
But their crushing defeats at Newcastle, where they lost 5-0, and Southampton in the space of a week must have dented the confidence of the Old Trafford giants.
